note: Tracked streamdb performance baseline. Metrics are CALIB-NORMALIZED (metric_ns_per_op / calib_ns_per_op measured in the SAME process/run), not raw ns/op — calib_ns_per_op is a fixed, streamdb-free integer workload the harness measures alongside the streamdb metrics (see crates/pillar-streamdb/examples/perf_bench.rs). Dividing by it cancels out this run's absolute CPU throughput (rig identity, thermal/frequency state, shared-sandbox contention/throttling), so a slower/faster sandbox does not itself register as a regression or as headroom. Recorded by the recurring streamdb-perf-benchmark discipline (ROI P1). The harness (scripts/streamdb-perf-benchmark.sh -> cargo run -p pillar-streamdb --example perf_bench --release, min-of-3 independent process invocations, each itself a min-of-3 in-process trials) compares a fresh measurement's ratios against these values with a regression tolerance (STREAMDB_PERF_TOLERANCE, default 1.40 = allow 40% noise on top of the calib normalization). A measurement worse than baseline*tolerance is a REGRESSION and fails the check unless a follow-up tuning task is filed. A measurement meaningfully BELOW baseline is headroom to record a new baseline. Update this file (and note it in the change doc) when a real, verified improvement lands. `calib_ns_per_op` here is fixed at 1.0 by convention (the baseline's own calibration unit); every other metric is stored already-divided-by-that-run's-calib, i.e. as a ratio.
